why: issue 2143 (RFC-0112 D2.2) -- the Tier 0 time-out: microseconds from now until the executor next needs to run (the `min` over the next wall timer, the backend's next internal event, a supervised route's deadline and every registered wake source -- the bound its own park uses), `None` when nothing is scheduled. For a host that owns the loop and drives the executor with `spin_some`. rclrs has no counterpart: its executor always owns the thread it waits on.
